title: Final campaign interpretation: AMI gain with broader regressions

data.title: Final campaign interpretation: AMI gain with broader regressions
paragraphs: The amended campaign and its matched frozen comparison are complete. The selected artifact remains the first production_all_audio fit, with no conditional refit. It completed three passes over 2,413,566 qualified train-plus-development microphone views: 7,240,698 visits and 517,569 updates in 34.29 active training hours. Repeated microphone views are not unique utterances. The exact first-production checkpoint identity and exported model are preserved; the longer reference pilot is evidence for retaining the recipe, not a replacement production model.

The frozen panel contains 512 clips, with 64 in each of eight cohorts. In the order base Whistle / initial tuned final export / final production / cached GigaSpeech, WER percentages are: AMI native 41.50 / 31.79 / 30.79 / 46.14; CHiME 6 native 71.45 / 63.23 / 66.43 / 71.73; CMU Arctic clean 12.59 / 12.06 / 12.59 / 5.77; HiFiTTS clean 3.41 / 3.96 / 4.84 / 1.76; HiFiTTS native 2.78 / 3.94 / 4.06 / 1.74; LibriSpeech clean 4.17 / 5.07 / 5.31 / 1.72; LibriSpeech native 11.73 / 13.81 / 14.26 / 6.14; VOiCES native 24.67 / 23.36 / 24.34 / 19.09. The generated comparison tables retain CER, runtime metrics and the distinct initial best export as well.

Relative to the initial tuned final export, production improves AMI by 0.99 percentage points but worsens the other seven cohorts, most visibly CHiME 6 by 3.20 points and VOiCES by 0.98 points. Relative to base Whistle it improves AMI, CHiME 6 and slightly VOiCES, ties CMU Arctic WER, and worsens both HiFiTTS and both LibriSpeech cohorts. Production beats cached GigaSpeech on AMI and CHiME 6 but trails it on the other six cohorts. These are measured domain tradeoffs; the final model is not a uniform accuracy improvement. No paired uncertainty interval for these frozen-test differences is supplied in the saved final summary, so small differences should not be presented as statistically established gains or losses.

The production model inserts zero words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. Its frozen-test quiet-audio summary contains zero marked clips and zero reference words, so it provides no final quiet-speech WER estimate. The development quiet results belong to the pilots and earlier models, not to an independent post-training age or quiet test of production. Energy thresholds reduce low-level contamination but do not guarantee intelligibility; the earlier audio audit quarantined near-silent speech and reserved CHiME annotations overlapping session seconds 0-1.

Production model path: C:\Users\amiri\Documents\GitHub\just-peachy\training\whistle_followups_v1\runs\production_all_audio\whistle.final.cact. Its saved SHA256 is 96d9339d13eb8c16e677a9a737e5797a7f8d9999947d82289161a2c9539cec83 and its file size is 29,346,671 bytes. The initial tuned model remains at C:\Users\amiri\Documents\GitHub\just-peachy\training\whistle_age_robust_v1\whistle.final.cact; the initial best export remains alongside it. The original pretrained-base revision is 741118687e1f008f06d1351a402a731274789790. Cached GigaSpeech metrics are historical matched predictions, not a newly trained or remotely launched Giga model.

Retained training-data license provenance records Common Voice as CC0-1.0, AMI and VOiCES as CC-BY-4.0, and CHiME 6 as CC-BY-SA-4.0. CHiME 6 licensing was explicitly confirmed resolved by the user on 23 October 2026, with attribution records retained. The initial diagnostic checkpoints archived before the audio audit are distinct from the audited training and final production identities.

The final evidence does not include real product-microphone validation or an independent final age test, because development age data joined final training after recipe selection. Earlier limitations on the historical initial comparison, including VOiCES overlap, remain relevant. These bounded, single-seed comparisons do not establish an optimal mixture or broad deployment reliability. Production CPU timings were measured on the current Windows/WSL host; historical GigaSpeech latency is not directly comparable, and neither those timings nor the export size proves Raspberry Pi speed or memory suitability.

The next action is to preserve these models and findings and close the completed campaign; no additional training stage was selected. The report is published with its visual-layout limitation retained: no approved native renderer or connected Word session is available, and the earlier renderer setup was blocked by automatic approval review. Structural OOXML checks can establish package integrity but do not establish visual layout. This limitation does not prevent the completed training and analysis from being reported.
